motion.name: reveal
motion.value: opacity + translateY(20px) over 0.7s cubic-bezier(0.22, 1, 0.36, 1), staggered by calc(var(--i) * 70ms)
motion.purpose: Scroll entrance at MOTION_INTENSITY 5, driven by one IntersectionObserver in src/lib/reveal.js. Each element is unobserved the moment it lands. No scroll listener, no rAF, no animation library.

motion.name: state-transition
motion.purpose: Colour, background and border-color on buttons, filter chips, nav links, form fields, contact links and card titles. Buttons additionally translateY(1px) on :active.

motion.name: image-hover
motion.purpose: The only transform on imagery. Clipped by overflow: hidden on the shot, so it never affects layout.

motion.name: positive-gating
motion.purpose: Every transition AND the reveal's hidden start state are declared only inside this guard. A reduced-motion visitor is never sent a rule that has to be cancelled, and nothing is ever hidden that JavaScript has to rescue. The reduce block that also zeroes transitions is belt-and-braces; nothing depends on it.

components.name: Project Footprints
components.description: The portfolio's whole layout system. Five footprints -- F1 band, F2 right, F3 left, F4 minor, and a coda used once -- that differ ONLY in CSS grid placement. Every one renders the identical DOM order (meta, title, screenshot, text, actions), so composition can vary widely while keyboard and screen-reader order never diverge from reading order. Imagery bleeds through the fluid gutter; F1 and the coda bleed both sides. Each footprint carries a trailing 1fr row so slack collects there instead of spreading the text column against a taller image. Below 980px all five collapse to the same single column and the rhythm is carried by aspect ratio alone.

components.name: Bleed Utilities
components.description: The mechanism the entire project system is built on. One fluid gutter token controls every edge-bleed on the site, so imagery reaching the viewport edge is a system behaviour rather than a per-component exception. html and body carry overflow-x: clip so a deliberate edge-crop can never produce a horizontal scrollbar.
components.css: :root { --gut: clamp(20px, 4vw, 72px); --container: 1560px; } .ds-container { max-width: var(--container); margin: 0 auto; padding: 0 var(--gut); } .ds-bleed-r { margin-right: calc(var(--gut) * -1); } .ds-bleed-l { margin-left: calc(var(--gut) * -1); } .ds-bleed-x { margin-left: calc(var(--gut) * -1); margin-right: calc(var(--gut) * -1); } html, body { overflow-x: clip; }

narrative.overview: The site is a hiring surface for a technical practitioner, and it argues in two registers at once. The first is structural: failure patterns from years of Tier 2/3 escalations, each answered by the mechanism built so that pattern cannot recur. The second is evidential: real product screenshots, at real scale, so a visitor who reads nothing still sees shipped software. Editorial Spatial is the language that carries both. It behaves like a printed publication rather than a web template -- a wide measure, a fluid gutter that imagery is allowed to break through, display type running from 12px to 138px, and deliberate voids that give a statement room to land. Variance is high but systematic: every asymmetry comes from a named footprint or a declared offset, never from hand-placement. Two things it deliberately is not. It is not agency-portfolio styling: no rotated navigation, no scroll hijack, no marquee, no locale strip, no section-number eyebrows. And it is not a cockpit: no gauges, no KPI tiles, no pseudo-telemetry, no fake instrumentation. The register is a well-run engineering organisation's document that happens to be beautifully set.
keyCharacteristics: Genuine product screenshots are a primary visual material, not decoration
Five compositional footprints over one invariant DOM order
A fluid gutter that imagery bleeds through; a 1560px container
Zero shadows and zero radii; depth comes from bleeds, scale and voids
One accent colour, held under roughly 5% of any viewport
Breakpoints derived from where the grid actually breaks
Touch targets keyed to pointer capability, not viewport width

rules.name: The Two-Token Boundary Rule
rules.body: Rule (#CFC7B8) and Boundary (#7C7364) are not interchangeable. Rule is decorative only and carries no contrast claim (1.45:1 on paper). Boundary is the identifying edge of an interactive control and clears WCAG 1.4.11 at 4.04:1. A control bounded only by Rule is a defect.

rules.name: The One Warm Value Rule
rules.body: Accent (#8A2B18, oxblood) is the only non-neutral in the system and is never used for a surface, a body of text, or more than about 5% of a viewport. It appears on index numerals, Live, the active nav underline, the mechanism marker, skill-group labels, the drop cap, the thesis rule and focus rings. Nowhere else.

rules.name: The Ink-Not-Accent Figure Rule
rules.body: The one source-backed operations figure is set in Ink at display scale, not Accent. At 124px an oxblood numeral would exceed the accent budget and read as a dashboard metric tile, which is the exact thing the rail was rebuilt to stop being.

rules.name: The No-Lighter-Grey Rule
rules.body: Graphite is the floor for text. Anything that would need a paler grey to read correctly is instead made smaller, moved, or deleted.

rules.name: The Mono-Is-Never-Prose Rule
rules.body: Martian Mono sets identifiers only -- eyebrows, section markers, category, status, dates, field headers, attributions, navigation. It never sets a sentence.

rules.name: The 12px Floor
rules.body: No text anywhere is smaller than 12px. Status and date are text, never a badge: currency is part of the evidence and should be readable rather than decorative.

rules.name: The One DOM Order Rule
rules.body: Every project footprint renders the identical order -- meta, title, screenshot, text, actions -- and differs only in CSS grid placement. Art direction on the outside, one predictable skeleton inside, so keyboard and screen-reader order can never diverge from reading order however unusual the composition looks.

rules.name: The Single-Gutter Rule
rules.body: Every bleed is measured against --gut: clamp(20px, 4vw, 72px). One token controls the whole edge behaviour of the site, and overflow-x: clip on html and body guarantees a deliberate edge-crop can never produce a horizontal scrollbar.

rules.name: The Composed Void Rule
rules.body: Empty space is a material. The paired reasoning block leaves roughly half the width empty at 1920 on purpose, and the thesis balances it from the opposite side. Voids are composed, not left over, and are not to be tightened merely because they are unusual.

rules.name: The Capability Rule
rules.body: Touch target sizing is keyed to (pointer: coarse), not viewport width. A tablet in portrait is wider than any phone breakpoint and still finger-driven.

rules.name: The Positive Motion Gate
rules.body: Every transition and the reveal's hidden start state are declared only inside @media (prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference). A reduced-motion visitor is never sent a rule that has to be cancelled, and nothing is ever hidden that JavaScript then has to rescue -- the page is fully composed with scripting off.

rules.name: The Painted-Pixel Rule
rules.body: Image verification must probe painted pixels, never intrinsic dimensions. A tiled AVIF reports a correct naturalWidth, raises no load error, logs nothing, and paints a blank rectangle. naturalWidth > 0 cannot detect it.

dos: Reach for an existing footprint before inventing a composition
Let imagery bleed through the gutter; that is the system, not an exception
Keep the accent under roughly 5% of any viewport
Declare motion inside the positive no-preference guard
Re-derive a sizes hint whenever a slot's column split changes
